clue.text: Lind's story about satisfied serving men

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the following pieces

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib
to have met a demand is to have satisfied it
RE, the Royal Engineers, are men serving in the British Army

explanation.surface: Jenny Lind's tale concerns the contented waiters who looked after her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lind' looks like the singer Jenny Lind, but it is an old word for the tree; the 's stands for 'is'. 'about' puts MET and RE inside LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lind is an archaic name, still found in German Linde, for the linden, a broadleaf shade tree.

clue.text: Not effectively hit, see!

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
Ely is a cathedral city, and a see is a bishop's seat

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a weak blow: look, that was a feeble hit!
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not an exclamation but a bishop's see: ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a feeble, unconvincing way is doing it without real effect.

clue.text: The Frenchwoman earned about a thousand

indicators.note: about means the word for earned goes around the other letters

parts.note: earned money is money made
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A French lady was paid roughly a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and M inside MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French form of address for a married woman, so it stands for a woman of France.

clue.text: Reduce the volume of refuse

explanation.surface: Lower the sound on the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering a dial on a radio is one sense of the phrasal verb; rejecting an offer is the other.

clue.text: Has a meal in a café at some expense

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of words café at some

explanation.surface: Someone dines out at a café and pays for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the answer sits within 'cafE AT Some'; 'expense' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is simply to consume food, a plain synonym.

clue.text: A choir-leader may turn corrupt

parts.note: may in the sense of being able, so can

indicators.note: turn means the word for corrupt is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to rot is to decay or become corrupt

explanation.surface: A choirmaster might go bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like a change of character, but it is the signal to read the word for corrupt backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor leads the singing in a synagogue or a church choir, a precentor.

clue.text: Old man cracking a nut

indicators.note: cracking means the letters of old man break apart and reform

explanation.surface: An elderly man splits open a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like breaking a nut, but it is the anagram signal for OLD MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is the edible kernel of a stone fruit, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Thespians can do it without going to pot!

definitions.text: Thespians can do it without going to pot!

parts.words: Thespians can do it without going to pot!
parts.note: actors respond to a prompt in the script, whereas a snooker player picks up his stick to pot a ball; here the stage sense needs no pot

explanation.surface: Actors manage this without going to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pot' means going to ruin, but also hints at potting a ball in snooker, where you would pick up the stick of the same name as an actor's prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor responds to a prompt line by coming in on time, the stage idiom.

clue.text: Edge into disunited dwelling

indicators.note: into means the word for edge goes inside the other word

parts.note: rent means torn apart, split, disunited
a side is an edge of something

explanation.surface: Someone sidles into a divided household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disunited' looks like a description of the household, but it supplies the word for torn apart, which 'into' then opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Resident as an adjective means living in a place, an exact synonym of the participle.

clue.text: A way speed can be controlled

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: This is a method for keeping one's pace in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' only links the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate as an adjective means restrained, kept within reasonable limits.

clue.text: The ass on board likes a cigarette

indicators.note: being on board a ship means placed inside the abbreviation for a steamship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the vessel one boards
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey aboard ship enjoys a quick cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS (steamship); MOKE is a British slang word for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually lights up tobacco is fond of it, the verb in its third person form.

clue.text: Show leaf to a conservationist body

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
NT is the National Trust, which preserves British heritage sites

explanation.surface: Hand over a sheet of paper to a heritage charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public spectacle or procession, a type of show.

clue.text: Writing a youngster many a letter from Greece

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep, a youngster
D is the Roman numeral for 500, so many

explanation.surface: A child writes plenty of letters from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a common crossword stand-in for 'many'; 'Writing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Wins support when opposed

parts.note: to win something is to gain it
aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Someone gains backing when facing opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so the past form means spoken against.

clue.text: A port (large) is ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of large is are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A big harbour is put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital of Algeria and a major Mediterranean harbour city.

clue.text: Sell now maybe, being affected by inflation

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of sell now could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Advice to sell immediately because prices are rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' looks economic, but the answer is puffed up physically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something puffed up with air or fluid has expanded, the literal sense of inflated.

clue.text: Fire-water

explanation.surface: Strong spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire-water' looks like strong spirits; it is two definitions. A burn is also Scottish for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To set alight or blaze is one sense; a burn is a Scottish word for a stream, the other.

clue.text: Civil spoken casual worker put first

indicators.note: put first means the worker comes ahead of the word for spoken

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A polite oral exchange with a casual employee taking priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Civil' looks like polite, but it means secular, as opposed to spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal means worldly or secular, relating to civil rather than church matters.

clue.text: Freebooters set it down — and up

parts.note: a set of people or musicians is a band
the word it is taken as written

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, means the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the same word it, used again

explanation.surface: Robbers put something down and then pick it back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is used twice: once written down as IT, then 'up' turns it to TI. 'and' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian-style plural of bandit, so robbers or plundering outlaws.

clue.text: The writer of "lying in the sun"

explanation.surface: Who wrote the poem about sunbathing?
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning was a Victorian poet; the quotation marks dress the second definition up as a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning was a nineteenth-century English poet; also, sunbathing turns skin a tan colour.

clue.text: Key to a hold-up in northern Holland

parts.note: E is a musical key
a dam holds up water

explanation.surface: A clue to a robbery in the north of the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' looks like a robbery; it is a barrier holding water back. The definition describes a town found in North Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a town in the Dutch province of North Holland, famous for its cheese.

clue.text: She could be in rags, with nothing coming in

indicators.note: coming in means the letter for nothing goes inside the rearranged letters
could be suggests the letters of in rags may be rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A woman might be dressed in tatters with no money arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges IN RAGS to SIGNRA, and 'coming in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, so a lady.

clue.text: Getting caught in the panic is unusual

indicators.note: in means the letter for caught is placed inside the word for panic

parts.note: a scare is a panic or alarm
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Being trapped in a stampede is a rare event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, hence rare and seldom seen.

clue.text: Fussy academic's huff about a newspaper leader

indicators.note: about means the word for huff surrounds the editor's letters

parts.note: to huff is to puff or pant
ED, editor, is the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A fussy scholar is annoyed about a newspaper's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huff' looks like a sulk, but it means panting; 'leader' looks like an editorial, but is the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone obsessed with minor rules and details of learning.

clue.text: Rise as about to close

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: Something climbs as it nears its conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up, climb or mount.

clue.text: Basic personal treatment

parts.note: basic suggests the base of the body, so care given to the feet and toenails

explanation.surface: Elementary self-care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic' looks like simple or elementary; it means at the base, the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: This beauty treatment is cosmetic care of the feet and toenails.

clue.text: Bearing with little back-street suckers

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for street is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Gullible people found with a small back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' looks like a side road; 'back' turns ST into TS. 'suckers' looks like dupes, but means boiled sweets you suck.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery like lollipops and boiled candies is sucked, a playful descriptive sense.

clue.text: Stop an animal feeding on fish

explanation.surface: Halt a fish-eating creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To close something up tight is to stop it; a seal is a marine mammal that eats fish.

clue.text: Answer sharply still

explanation.surface: Reply curtly yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb, but it is the noun: a distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp riposte is one sense; the other is the glass vessel used in a distillery.

clue.text: Get up to present an old patriarch with some pictures

parts.note: Levi, son of Jacob, was a biblical patriarch
the Tate is a London art gallery, a collection of pictures

explanation.surface: Rise to give an ancient elder some paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the national art gallery group in Britain; 'Get up' means rise into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to rise or float in the air, as in a magic act.

clue.text: Delay to rile constituents

indicators.note: constituents treats the letters of to rile as parts to be reassembled

explanation.surface: Stalling to annoy voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters, but it signals rearranging TO RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger or dawdle, wasting time.

clue.text: Quietly came down as promised

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a bird that lighted on a branch came down on it

explanation.surface: Someone softly descended as agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight one's troth is to pledge one's word in marriage.
